sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Why the recordings are protected
sections.what: The module docstring explains why the test fixture must never be overwritten and how live output is organised by provider and model.
sections.why: A live run could overwrite the baseline without any error, so the rule is enforced in code, not left to review.
sections.watch_out: Recording by provider and model keeps two runs from replacing each other.

sections.name: SyntheticRecordingsAreReadOnly
sections.title: Read-only error
sections.what: Defines the error raised when a live run asks to write into the synthetic fixture or a replay asks to record.
sections.why: A redirect would send output to a different place than the caller expects, which makes missing recordings hard to trace.
sections.watch_out: The error is meant to stop the run, so catching it and continuing would defeat the protection.

sections.name: slug
sections.title: Name cleaning
sections.what: Turns a provider or model name into a safe folder name, and refuses names that become empty.
sections.why: Model names contain slashes, and dots could climb out of the folder. Cleaning both stops the path from escaping.
sections.watch_out: Two different names can clean to the same folder, so distinct models could share output.

sections.name: is_synthetic
sections.title: Synthetic path check
sections.what: Reports whether a path is inside the synthetic folder, after resolving links and dot-dot parts.
sections.why: Checking the resolved path, not the typed path, catches links and tricks that would otherwise slip past.
sections.watch_out: The check depends on the resolved path, so the resolution has to be correct for the platform.

sections.name: guard_write
sections.title: Write guard
sections.what: Returns the path if the write is allowed, and raises the read-only error if it is a live run aimed at the fixture.
sections.why: Returning the path means the caller must go through the guard to get it. An assert could be forgotten.
sections.watch_out: The guard only checks when the live flag is true.

sections.name: recording_sink
sections.title: Recording sink
sections.what: The one function that hands out a folder for captured output. It refuses replay runs and empty case ids.
sections.why: A replay has nothing new to capture, and a replay that wrote output would overwrite its own source.
sections.watch_out: Any new way of writing output must go through this function, or the protection does not apply.

summary: Decides where a live run may save the model output it captured, and refuses any write into the authored test fixture.
purpose: Protect the synthetic recordings from being overwritten by a live run, since they are pinned to the test baseline.
why: The docstring explains that an overwrite would not fail loudly. Replay would still match itself, but against a different answer, so the protection is enforced in code.
how: A recording sink is the only way to get a write folder. It requires a live run, a case id, and a provider and model name, each cleaned to a safe folder name. The write guard then refuses any path inside the synthetic folder.
inputs: A provider name, a model name, a case id, and a flag saying whether the run is live.
outputs: A folder path under the live folder, or an error.
risks: A path that escapes the live folder through unusual characters could reach the synthetic tree. The slug function is meant to prevent this. Only callers that use the sink are protected.
debug: If a write is refused, read the message, which names the path and the allowed location. If a folder name is odd, check the slug output. An empty name raises an error.
